title: A Combined Content Addressable Memory and In-Memory Processing Approach for k-Clique Counting Acceleration
problem: Current k-Clique counting accelerators suffer from high data transfer overhead caused by intensive set intersection operations and inability to achieve effective load balancing. These bottlenecks prevent accelerators from meeting performance requirements in graph mining applications.
motivation: k-Clique counting is a critical graph mining operation with growing applications, but existing accelerators fail to deliver adequate performance at scale.
method: The solution pairs specialized hardware with smart scheduling. Content Addressable Memory (CAM)—a search technique that works directly on data without moving it—first narrows down which graph vertices must be counted. Processing-In-Memory (PIM)—computation done inside memory chips rather than at a separate processor—then counts the cliques in parallel using repeated Boolean AND operations (finding which vertices appear in multiple sets). Dynamic scheduling distributes the counting work evenly across all PIM chips, ensuring none sits idle.
key_novelty: Combining CAM (a search technique that doesn't move data) and PIM (in-memory computation) with dynamic scheduling eliminates the data transfer bottleneck by doing both search-space reduction and parallel k-clique counting right where the data lives.
contributions: Hybrid CAM-PIM architecture specifically designed for k-Clique counting acceleration
CAM-based binary induced subgraph generation to reduce search space and data movement
Dynamic task scheduling strategies for near-optimal load balancing in PIM arrays
Achieved 167.5× speedup over CPU and 28.8× over GPU with 788.3× energy efficiency improvement
primary_theme: Memory-system codesign for graph algorithm acceleration
